cleanIntro:
The Vector Gen 3 is a closed-bolt, delayed-blowback pistol-calibre gun that feeds from full-size Glock magazines. It comes apart on four takedown pins: three let the upper housing lift off the lower, and the fourth — reached with the receiver turned upside down — releases the bolt and slider assembly. The same book covers the SDP, SBR and CRB; only the carbine's barrel shroud adds a step.

KRISS's interval is a wipe-down and light oil of the bolt and slider raceways every 400 rounds, and a full teardown, clean and inspection at least every 1,000 rounds — sooner in dust and humidity. Two things the book forbids: releasing the hammer while the upper is off the receiver, and taking the fire control group apart.

steps.title: Finger outside the guard, safety on
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction for the whole procedure. Take your finger out of the trigger guard and put the safety on before you do anything else.
steps.prose: Every step after this is done with hands near the action. Start from a gun that cannot fire by a slip.
steps.quote: When finished firing, ALWAYS place your finger outside the trigger guard with the barrel maintained in safe direction and activate the safety.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Unloading and Clearing, printed p.10

steps.title: Magazine out first
steps.action: Press the magazine release and pull the magazine out of the well. If it will not come, check that your support hand is not holding it in place.
steps.prose: Clearing the chamber with a magazine still in only chambers the next round.
steps.quote: Press the magazine release and remove the magazine.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Unloading and Clearing, printed p.10

steps.title: Charging handle: turn it 90°, then pull and HOLD
steps.action: Rotate the charging handle 90 degrees and grip it close to the receiver. Pull it fully to the rear and keep holding it there — any chambered round comes out of the ejection port.
steps.prose: The handle has to be turned before it will draw the bolt back; gripping it near the receiver keeps your hand from slipping off under the spring load.
steps.quote: Rotate the charging handle 90 degrees and grip it as close to the receiver as possible. Pull and hold the charging handle to the rear.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Unloading and Clearing, printed p.10

steps.title: LOOK into the chamber, then let go — and SAFE
steps.action: Still holding the handle back, look through the ejection port and see an empty chamber. Only then release the charging handle, and switch the firearm to Safe. Empty the magazine before it goes anywhere near the gun again.
steps.prose: Hearing a round fall out is not the check. Seeing the empty chamber is.
steps.quote: Look through the ejection port and visually confirm that the chamber is clear of ammunition. Release the charging handle.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Unloading and Clearing, printed p.10

steps.title: Charge it once to reset the hammer — bolt home
steps.action: Pull the charging handle back to cock the hammer, then let the bolt go forward so it is fully in battery before any pin comes out.
steps.prose: The upper must come off with the hammer cocked. Released with the housings apart, the hammer can damage the ejection port.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle back to reset the hammer.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Disassembly, printed p.18

steps.title: First three takedown pins out
steps.action: Push out the first three of the four takedown pins. Leave the fourth in for now — it holds the bolt and slider assembly in the receiver and is reached from underneath.
steps.prose: Keep the pins together; the book has you inspect all four afterwards.
steps.quote: Remove the first 3 take down pins
steps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Disassembly, printed p.18

steps.title: ⚠ Upper straight up, lower straight down
steps.action: Separate the housings by pulling the upper housing straight up and the lower housing straight down. Do not rock them apart. From here until reassembly, do NOT let the hammer fall — no trigger pulls on the separated upper.
steps.prose: Straight apart keeps the housings from levering against each other.
steps.caution: Do not release the hammer when the upper has been separated from the recevier, doing so could cause damage to the ejection port.
steps.quote: Separate the housings by pulling straight up on the upper housing and down on the lower housing.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Disassembly, printed p.18

steps.title: Receiver upside down — fourth pin out
steps.action: Turn the receiver upside down and remove the fourth and final takedown pin.
steps.prose: This pin is what secures the bolt and slider assembly; with it out, the assembly is free to come out of its channels.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Disassembly, printed p.19

steps.title: Bolt and slider out as one assembly
steps.action: Pull the bolt and slider assembly out of the receiver together.
steps.prose: Note how the bolt lugs and the slider rails sit in their channels as it comes out — that is the order they go back in.
steps.quote: Pull the bolt and slider assembly out of the receiver.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Disassembly, printed p.19

steps.title: Rotate the bolt off the slider
steps.action: Rotate the bolt and separate it from the slider assembly. This is the last disassembly step the book gives.
steps.prose: The bolt only leaves the slider by rotating — do not pry it.
steps.quote: Rotate the bolt and separate it from the slider assembly.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Disassembly, printed p.19

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: the upper housing with the fire control group, the lower housing, the bolt, the slider assembly and the four takedown pins. That is the whole of KRISS's disassembly. DEEP CLEAN carries the book's inspection checks for the bolt, extractor, firing pin and slider, the carbine's barrel shroud, and its stopping point at the FCG.
steps.prose: When it goes back together, the bolt lugs and the slider rails each have their own channel — get that wrong and the book says the gun is damaged.
steps.quote: When reinstalling the bolt and slider assembly into the receiver, ensure that the lugs for both the slider and the bolt are inserted into their respective channels. Incorrect assembly will lead to damage.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Disassembly, printed p.19

deepSteps.title: CRB only — barrel shroud off
deepSteps.action: On the carbine, remove the four flat socket cap screws with a 2.5 mm Allen key and slide the barrel shroud forward off the barrel. The SDP and SBR have no shroud — skip this step on those.
deepSteps.prose: Before the shroud goes back on, KRISS recommends a light film of oil on its o-ring.
deepSteps.quote: To remove the barrel shroud, loosen and remove the four flat socket cap screws using a 2.5mm Allen key, then slide the shroud off the barrel.
deepSteps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Cleaning and Inspection — Barrel Assembly (Carbine model), printed p.21

deepSteps.title: Carbon under the extractor
deepSteps.action: Clean the bolt face and dig the carbon out from under the extractor claw.
deepSteps.prose: This is the build-up the book singles out: it shows up as extraction and chambering trouble long before it looks bad.
deepSteps.quote: Fouling or build-up of carbon under the extractor may lead to poor extraction and poor chambering.
deepSteps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Cleaning and Inspection — Bolt, printed p.20

deepSteps.title: Extractor: cracks, chips, pivot pin
deepSteps.action: Look the extractor over for cracks or chips, and check its pivot pin has not walked out of its hole.
deepSteps.prose: A drifting pin lets the extractor shift; a chipped claw loses its grip on the rim.
deepSteps.quote: Ensure the extractor has no cracks or chips and that the extractor pivot pin has not drifted from its hole.
deepSteps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Cleaning and Inspection — Bolt, printed p.20

deepSteps.title: Extractor spring: thumb test
deepSteps.action: Push up on the bolt-face end of the extractor with your thumb. It should barely move and take real force to move at all. If it moves easily, the spring has weakened.
deepSteps.prose: Weak extractor tension is one of the book's listed causes of failure to extract.
deepSteps.quote: Check by pushing up on the forward (bolt face) end of the extractor with your thumb; it should only move slightly and require considerable force to move it at all.
deepSteps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Cleaning and Inspection — Bolt, printed p.20

deepSteps.title: Bolt face and firing pin
deepSteps.action: Check the bolt face for scoring or damage and that the area round the firing pin channel is clear. Then press the rear of the firing pin with a wooden dowel: it should move freely under very little pressure. Look at the tip — clean, not deformed.
deepSteps.prose: A fouled firing pin is one of the book's causes of a gun that will not fire.
deepSteps.quote: Check the firing pin by pressing on the rear using a wood dowel or similar tool to ensure it moves freely and easily.
deepSteps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Cleaning and Inspection — Bolt, printed p.20

deepSteps.title: Slider: guide-rod screw, rails, buffer
deepSteps.action: Check the retaining screw at the top of the spring guide rod is tight. Inspect the slider's bolt retaining rails for cracks, and the buffer for excessive wear.
deepSteps.prose: The rails carry the bolt; a crack there is not something to shoot through.
deepSteps.quote: Inspect the slider to ensure there are no cracks in the bolt retaining rails.
deepSteps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Cleaning and Inspection — Slider, printed p.21

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The FCG stays together — KRISS's stopping point
deepSteps.action: The fire control group in the upper housing is cleaned in place with swabs and a nylon brush. Do not take it apart or modify it. That is as far as the book goes.
deepSteps.prose: Anything the FCG needs beyond cleaning is not owner work in this book.
deepSteps.quote: Do not attempt to disassemble or modify the FCG. Doing so may cause malfunctions or degraded performance, and will void your warranty.
deepSteps.cite: KRISS Vector Gen III (SDP / SBR / CRB) — Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Cleaning and Inspection — Upper Housing, printed p.22

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Patch wet with solvent in the eyelet on the bore cable; feed the cable in at the chamber and pull it all the way out of the muzzle. Repeat 2–3 times with a fresh wet patch each time.
Swap the eyelet for the brush adaptor; feed it in at the chamber and pull it through the muzzle 2–3 times.
Patches again, as the first pass, to lift the fouling the brush loosened.
Carbine: lightly oil the barrel shroud o-ring before the shroud goes back on.

cleaning.name: BOLT AND SLIDER
tasks: Bolt face clean and free of carbon, especially under the extractor.
Area round the firing pin channel clear of build-up.
Wipe the bolt and slider raceways with a lint-free cloth.
Thin coat of oil on the bolt lugs; one drop on the extractor pivot pin.

cleaning.name: UPPER HOUSING AND FCG
tasks: Wipe the upper housing with patches or a lint-free cloth.
Cotton swab or nylon brush into the fire control group.
Ejection port mounting screws tight.
Ambidextrous fire/safe lever screws tight, with a positive click as the lever is switched back and forth.
FCG and frame tight in the housing and free of debris.
Two drops of oil on the hammer pivot pin, one on the trigger pivot pin. Thumb pressure rearward on the hammer, hold the trigger, ease the hammer forward and back several times to spread the oil.
⛔ Never let the hammer fall freely with the upper off the receiver — it can damage the ejection port.
⛔ Do not disassemble or modify the FCG.

cleaning.name: LOWER HOUSING
tasks: Clean it as you cleaned the upper housing.
Housing screws tight; bolt catch/release lever mounting-block screws tight.
Charging handle moves freely; its two return springs intact and clean.
Magazine release button moves freely, area underneath clear.
Ejector not loose, bent or chipped.
Two to three drops of oil in each of the left and right slider raceways; thin coat on the slider bolt raceway.
Two drops on the charging handle assembly; cycle it to spread the oil.

cleaning.name: TAKEDOWN PINS
tasks: All four pins undamaged.
Retaining spring intact and undamaged.
Clean each pin as needed.

reassembly: Rotate the bolt back into the slider. Check the bolt is oriented correctly and the bolt-and-slider assembly is properly together before it goes in.
Receiver upside down: bolt lugs into the FORWARD channel, slider rails into the REARMOST channel. Slide the whole assembly into position.
Secure it with its takedown pin.
⛔ Hammer locked back before the upper goes on.
Mate the upper assembly to the receiver and replace the remaining takedown pins.
Carbine: lightly oil the shroud o-ring, slide the shroud on and refit its four screws.
Muzzle in a safe direction — run the function check before the gun is loaded.
fncheck: Magazine OUT and the gun confirmed clear first. Charge the Vector, point it in a safe direction and pull the trigger: you should hear the hammer release and strike the firing pin. Keep the trigger held, charge the gun again, then let the trigger out slowly — there should be an audible click as it resets. Do it once more. Finally charge it, put it on Safe and try the trigger: it must be locked and the hammer must not fall. A trigger that does not reset is one of KRISS's listed faults — weak sear return spring, a fouled FCG, or a damaged hammer spring — and goes to a KRISS Certified Dealer or KRISS USA.
